content.title: About
content.content: Pad Thai with meat is a popular Thai dish made from rice noodles stir‑fried with egg, soy sauce, tamarind, lime, peanuts and pieces of meat (usually chicken, pork or beef). The dish balances sweet‑sour, salty and mildly spicy flavors and is aromatic with fresh herbs and lime.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pad Thai is considered Thailand's national dish and is often served at street stalls.
Tamarind, the key ingredient of the sauce, gives the dish its distinctive tangy‑sweet taste.
Traditionally the dish is garnished with lime wedges, bean sprouts and crushed peanuts.
Original recipes use rice noodles 5‑7 mm wide, but regional variations may use thinner or wider strands.
The dish is typically cooked over high heat in a wok to achieve a slightly charred, crunchy texture.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Rice noodles supply steady energy through slowly released glucose.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tamarind and soy sauce contain vitamin B6 and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Peanuts add monounsaturated fats that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Lime and fresh herbs such as cilantro are rich in vitamin C and flavonoids that combat free radicals.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are a common allergen; those with a peanut allergy should avoid the dish or use a substitute.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce and tamarind paste can be salty, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten in soy sauce
items.content: Traditional soy sauce contains wheat; gluten‑free versions are needed for celiac disease.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: The dish is often served with chili; sensitive individuals should reduce the amount of spice.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Pad Thai hot, sprinkled with crushed peanuts, fresh cilantro, lime wedges and, if desired, chili powder. Additional vegetables such as carrots or bean sprouts can be added to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Pad Thai is best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. When reheating, add a splash of water to prevent the noodles from drying out.
